news.title: World Cup: Argentina mark England win with National Football Teams Day
news.lede: Argentina shatter England's World Cup dreams in semi-final. The Argentine Football Association, external has announced 15 July will be 'National Football Teams Day' to mark Argentina's 2026 World Cup semi-final victory over England on that date. Bidding for their first World Cup final since 1966, England took the lead in a tense affair in Atlanta through a 55th-minute Anthony Gordon finish. But with Thomas Tuchel's side sitting deep, Argentina struck in the 85th and 92nd minutes to break English hearts and claim a 2-1 win.

news.title: Netflix reports 250% rise in football content views during FIFA World Cup 2026
news.lede: "Netflix said viewership of its football-related content more than doubled during the FIFA 2026 Men's World Cup, as the streaming platform highlighted audience engagement across documentaries, series, talk shows and games ahead of its coverage of the FIFA 2027 Women's World Cup in the US and Canada. Weekly views of its football titles in May increased by more than 250% compared with the weekly average between January and April. The platform"s football slate included documentaries and series such as Brazil '70: The Third Star, México 86, Colombia's James and Norway: The Dark Horse, along with the official FIFA World Cup: Launch Edition video game. In Brazil, views of Ronaldinho: The One and Only increased 34% in the hours following Ronaldinho's halftime appearance during the tournament.

news.title: FIFA denies Morocco deal for 2030 World Cup final
news.lede: FIFA has decisively quashed rumors of a secret agreement with Morocco to host the 2030 World Cup final at Benslimane stadium. Wednesday, a spokesperson for the global football authority dismissed earlier reports published by The Times, which had been widely circulated in the media. «Assertions that the FIFA president has committed to any specific location for the 2030 World Cup final are false and misleading. FIFA will make its decision in due time», the spokesperson told EFE.

news.title: Gianni Infantino: FIFA leaders back under-fire president following crisis meeting as he apologises for 'mistakes' over World Cup sell-off
news.lede: Under-fire FIFA president Gianni Infantino has shaken off calls to resign - for now - with the backing of the governing body's leaders, though apologised for "mistakes" in his botched attempts to sell off a stake in the World Cup. In a statement released after seven hours of crisis talks in Morocco, FIFA said its management board had reaffirmed their "full support" for Infantino - including secretary general Mattias Grafstrom, only days after he had labelled the World Cup plans "a sad and reproachable series of events". The pair were later seen laughing together watching a Women's AFCON game in Rabat. Infantino had faced mounting calls to resign following the leak of previously undiscussed proposals, after it was revealed national associations had not been consulted and had been given a deadline barely a month away in mid-September and the promise of a £30.1m incentive to back them .

news.title: Messi sizzles with record double in first start since World Cup final
news.lede: Lionel Messi became the all-time leading scorer in the Leagues Cup after netting twice in Inter Miami's 4-2 victory over Atlético de San Luis today (Bangladesh time) in the 2026 edition's opening group matches. The Argentine superstar cancelled out the visitors' early opener in the 11th minute, finishing from Noah Allen's pass before Telasco Segovia put Miami ahead. Messi struck again just before half-time, once more converting an Allen assist, to take his Leagues Cup tally to 14 goals -- the most in the competition's history. Messi had helped Inter Miami win the 2023 Leagues Cup shortly after joining the club.

news.title: Oliver Baumann says Julian Nagelsmann apologized after World Cup benching
news.lede: Germany goalkeeper Oliver Baumann has opened up about one of the toughest moments of his career after Julian Nagelsmann opted to restore Manuel Neuer as the starting goalkeeper for the World Cup. Baumann had established himself as Germany’s No. 1 leading up to the tournament, but Nagelsmann, leaning on input from some key players, ultimately turned back to Neuer for football’s biggest stage. While the decision was undoubtedly disappointing for Baumann, the goalkeeper sayid that the ex-Germany coach, who was recently replaced by Jürgen Klopp, reached out afterward to discuss everything openly. “He [Nagelsmann] was sorry about how everything turned out in the end.

news.title: How to fix Fifa: what can be done to salvage football’s beleaguered governing body?
news.lede: Gianni Infantino followed World Cup controversies with a widely scorned plan to let private investors in. Here’s how the game’s leaders can find a path forward. How can an organisation that runs the biggest sporting event in the world also be the one that sets the rules for the entire game? We saw the reality of such a conflict at the recent World Cup as Fifa ran roughshod over its rulebook – be it over the length of suspensions or the duration of half-time – in an attempt to generate more attention for its competition.
